{"agent_version": "0.14.0", "task": "Implement `crc.py` in pure Python (standard library only; the suite blocks
`zlib` and `binascii`) so that `python -m pytest tests -q` passes.

- `crc32(data: bytes) -> int`: the standard CRC-32 (IEEE 802.3, polynomial
  0xEDB88320 reflected), the same function as `zlib.crc32`. The suite holds
  it to the published check values.

same length, `crc32(a ^ b) == crc32(a) ^ crc32(b)` (bytewise xor). Any
correct implementation must satisfy every test.

crc32(b) ^ crc32(bytes(n)), with the same seeds and length range.
    running-value  crc32(data, value=0, /) continues a running CRC: crc32(b, crc32(a)) == crc32(a + b) for any split, including empty pieces.
    buffer-types  bytes, bytearray, memoryview, and array.array('B'/'I') of the same bytes give identical CRCs. A str argument raises TypeError.
    result-range  Every return value is a plain int in [0, 2**32), whatever the input or starting value (including value >= 2**31).
    combine  crc32_combine(crc1, crc2, len2) satisfies crc32_combine(crc32(a), crc32(b), len(b)) == crc32(a + b) without reading the data. It returns crc1 when len2 == 0 and raises ValueError when len2 < 0.
    cli-output  `python crc.py FILE...` prints one line per file in the form `%08x  name` (lowercase hex, 8 digits, two spaces) and exits 0. With no arguments or with `-` it reads stdin and prints the name `-`.
    cli-errors  A missing or unreadable file writes a one-line error to stderr, doesn't stop the remaining files, and makes the process exit with status 1.
    streaming-perf  The CLI reads files in fixed-size chunks (64 KiB), never the whole file at once, and crc32 handles 1 MiB in under 2 s on CPython.
    extra-tests-exist  Everything that ships beyond the original suite (running value, buffer types, TypeError, combine, CLI) has at least one test in tests/, and those tests run under the same zlib-blocking conftest.
